subject: generator name string: off by one error?

messages.author: bff9e4feca8b059f
messages.subject: generator name string: off by one error?
parts:
I'm getting a very odd behavior where I'm using the from(..., arrive=F) to setup a number of deactivated generators having names "site_patient1", "site_patient2" etc. When I run the simulation, I get this output:

0: site0: site startup: 2
0: site1: site startup: 23
1: site2: site startup: 81
1.18429: patient_site810:     patient enrolled 1.18429478887336
Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) : 
  Evaluation error: there is no arrival running.

There is both a site 81 (with a corresponding patient_site81 generator), and a site 810 (with a patient_site810 generator), but site 810 (and it's generator) are not supposed to start until time 216; so how can a patient_site810 be generated soon after site 81 (not 810) started? If I change the random seed, I see identical behavior (site 7 starts, then I get a site 70 patient generated, etc). And the evaluation error also seems to indicate some form of internal corruption. This smells like a C-level string length is off-by-one, and capturing the trailing null byte as an extra zero in the name.  Code is below for inspection; FYI if I remove the branch() statement that mucks with the patient_site generators' rates, I still get the same behavior, so it's not that (or at least not that alone).

  set.seed(1234)
  env <- simmer("Patient Enrollment")
  patient <- trajectory() %>%

    # do we actually still need more patients?
    branch(
      function() {
        ifelse(is.na(get_global(env,"count")) ||
                 get_global(env, "count") < N, 1, 0)
      },
      continue=T,
      trajectory() %>%
        log_(function() paste0("    patient enrolled ", as.character(now(env)))) %>%
        set_global("count", function() {
          count <- get_global(env, "count") + 1
          if (is.na(count)) count <- 1
          count
        })
    )
  
  # loop to add all the site-specific patient generators:
  for (i in 1:nrow(site_data)) {
    env %<>% add_generator(paste0("patient_site", site_data$Site[i]),
                           patient,
                           from(site_data$start[i],
                                function() rexp(1, site_data$rate[i]),
                                arrive=F))
  }
  
  site <- trajectory() %>%
    set_attribute("starttime", now(env)) %>%
    log_(function() paste0("site startup: ", get_attribute(env, "Site"))) %>%
    
    # modify rate of patient generator for this site:
    branch(function() { findInterval(runif(1), c(0,1,2,3)/3) }, continue=T,
           trajectory() %>% set_source(function() paste0("patient_site", get_attribute(env, "Site")),
                                       function() rexp(1, 0.5 * get_attribute(env, "rate"))),
           trajectory() %>% set_source(function() paste0("patient_site", get_attribute(env, "Site")),
                                       function() rexp(1, 1.0 * get_attribute(env, "rate"))),
           trajectory() %>% set_source(function() paste0("patient_site", get_attribute(env, "Site")),
                                       function() rexp(1, 1.5 * get_attribute(env, "rate")))
    )%>%
    timeout(30) %>% # wait for a ~month
    # keep going still?
    rollback(amount = 2, check=function() { get_global(env, "count") < N }) %>%
    # deactivate patient generator
    deactivate(function() paste0("patient_site", get_attribute(env, "Site")))
  
  env %<>%
    add_dataframe("site",
                  site,
                  site_data) %>%
    run()

> I'm getting a very odd behavior where I'm using the from(..., arrive=F) to setup a number of deactivated generators having names "site_patient1", "site_patient2" etc. When I run the simulation, I get this output:

> 0: site0: site startup: 2
> 0: site1: site startup: 23
> 1: site2: site startup: 81
> 1.18429: patient_site810: patient enrolled 1.18429478887336
> Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) :
> Evaluation error: there is no arrival running.
>
> There is both a site 81 (with a corresponding patient_site81 generator), and a site 810 (with a patient_site810 generator), but site 810 (and it's generator) are not supposed to start until time 216; so how can a patient_site810 be generated soon after site 81 (not 810) started?

Arrivals are automatically numbered. If you define a generator called
"patient_81", your first arrival will be "patient_810", the second
one, "patient_811" and so on. If you have a generated called
"patient_810", its first arrival will be "patient_8100". If you add an
underscore (e.g., "patient_81_") at the end of generators' names, it
will be easier to distinguish them.

> If I change the random seed, I see identical behavior (site 7 starts, then I get a site 70 patient generated, etc). And the evaluation error also seems to indicate some form of internal corruption. This smells like a C-level string length is off-by-one, and capturing the trailing null byte as an extra zero in the name.

There's no corruption, as I've explained. The error denotes that you
are trying to call an arrival method from a process that is not an
arrival, typically a generator. See below.

> Code is below for inspection; FYI if I remove the branch() statement that mucks with the patient_site generators' rates, I still get the same behavior, so it's not that (or at least not that alone).
>
> set.seed(1234)
> env <- simmer("Patient Enrollment")
> patient <- trajectory() %>%
>
> # do we actually still need more patients?
> branch(
> function() {
> ifelse(is.na(get_global(env,"count")) ||
> get_global(env, "count") < N, 1, 0)
> },
> continue=T,
> trajectory() %>%
> log_(function() paste0(" patient enrolled ", as.character(now(env)))) %>%
> set_global("count", function() {
> count <- get_global(env, "count") + 1
> if (is.na(count)) count <- 1
> count
> })
> )
>
> # loop to add all the site-specific patient generators:
> for (i in 1:nrow(site_data)) {
> env %<>% add_generator(paste0("patient_site", site_data$Site[i]),
> patient,
> from(site_data$start[i],
> function() rexp(1, site_data$rate[i]),
> arrive=F))
> }
>
> site <- trajectory() %>%
> set_attribute("starttime", now(env)) %>%
> log_(function() paste0("site startup: ", get_attribute(env, "Site"))) %>%
>
> # modify rate of patient generator for this site:
> branch(function() { findInterval(runif(1), c(0,1,2,3)/3) }, continue=T,
> trajectory() %>% set_source(function() paste0("patient_site", get_attribute(env, "Site")),
> function() rexp(1, 0.5 * get_attribute(env, "rate"))),
> trajectory() %>% set_source(function() paste0("patient_site", get_attribute(env, "Site")),
> function() rexp(1, 1.0 * get_attribute(env, "rate"))),
> trajectory() %>% set_source(function() paste0("patient_site", get_attribute(env, "Site")),
> function() rexp(1, 1.5 * get_attribute(env, "rate")))

You can't do this. You are setting a generator function, and you can't
retrieve an arrival's attribute there. This is what raises the error.

> )%>%
> timeout(30) %>% # wait for a ~month
> # keep going still?
> rollback(amount = 2, check=function() { get_global(env, "count") < N }) %>%
> # deactivate patient generator
> deactivate(function() paste0("patient_site", get_attribute(env, "Site")))
>
> env %<>%
> add_dataframe("site",
> site,
> site_data) %>%
> run()
>

Yes, I see my rookie mistake now, sorry again. Thanks for your patience.

I am still stuck figuring out how to change the rate of a given generator over time; to use your gas station example as a simpler example, how would you modify it to incorporate day/night (or hourly) fluctuations in vehicle arrival rates, I guess using from_to() with disjoint generators? I was hoping to have something more stochastic (flipping between states with different arrival rates, not at prespecified times but by some transition frequency).

thanks again,
-Aaron

-Aaron

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] generator name string: off by one error?
parts:
El vie., 15 jun. 2018 a las 19:20, Aaron Mackey (<ajma...@gmail.com>) escribió:
>
> Yes, I see my rookie mistake now, sorry again. Thanks for your patience.
>
> I am still stuck figuring out how to change the rate of a given generator over time; to use your gas station example as a simpler example, how would you modify it to incorporate day/night (or hourly) fluctuations in vehicle arrival rates, I guess using from_to() with disjoint generators? I was hoping to have something more stochastic (flipping between states with different arrival rates, not at prespecified times but by some transition frequency).

For prespecified times, from_to is the best option. If you want random
changes, you simply need to sample the time to the next change from
some distribution and apply the new rate based on the current
simulation time. Your generators can query the simulation time with
the "now" function ("get_attribute" is arrival-specific, but "now" can
be called anywhere).

Iñaki
